title: Adaptive client shims, staged deprecation plan, and cross-language interop testing playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD-style ticket to define requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for adaptive client 'shims' that provide backward-compatible behavior across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Goal: enable progressive deprecation of legacy pagination and streaming surface areas while preserving safety for production users via feature gates, automated interop tests, and server-side compatibility layers.
scope_changes: Initial scope included only pagination contract migration; expanded to include streaming API backcompat and retry semantics after early engineering spike revealed hidden coupling across SDKs.
Removed plan to add new transport-level wire protocol; instead will rely on SDK-side shims and server routing to reduce blast radius.
Added cross-language interop test harness and CI gating to block incompatible releases.
acceptance_criteria: All three SDKs (Python v3.x, TS v2.x, Go v1.x) expose the new 'AdaptiveFetch' surface while preserving existing method names as shims behind deprecation warnings.
Pagination: cursor- and offset-based flows must be interoperable with server cursor migration layer; fallbacks trigger within 100ms on average under normal load.
Streaming: clients must support chunked streaming and reconnection semantics; server must accept both legacy stream markers and new structured events without requiring client changes.

Retries: default retry behavior to be standardized (idempotency-aware, jittered exponential backoff) and documented; unit and e2e tests must assert no duplicate side-effects for non-idempotent routes.
Interop CI: every PR that changes SDK surfaces must run the interop matrix (Python/TS/Go) and pass all compatibility tests before merge.
Canary rollout: server-side routing with 1% traffic to new behavior for 48 hours with automated error/latency/regression alarms before broad rollout.
Migration docs: clear migration guide and code samples for each language published in docs site and referenced in SDK release notes.
Telemetry: telemetry hooks must emit version, shim-state, and migration-flag for 100% of calls for one week after rollout to measure adoption and failures.
decisions: Use SDK-side shims + server routing rather than a wire protocol change to minimize upgrade coordination for customers.
Deprecation cadence: 6-month deprecation window with automatic deprecation warnings baked into SDK logs and the Console usage page.
Testing: invest in a polyglot interop harness (containerized scenarios) that runs on PRs and nightly regression runs.

notes_for_engineering: Provide stable feature flag that can be toggled per-customer and per-route for staged rollouts.
Expose telemetry keys: sdk.name, sdk.version, shim.enabled, migration.flag.
Ensure binary releases include deprecation warning in first-run logs and a concise migration URL.
Test failure modes: partial upgrade (only server updated), partial client update (only one language updated), mixed-version clients in a single customer environment.
test_plan: Unit tests for shim behavior in each SDK covering normal/edge cursors, empty pages, and truncated streams.
Interop e2e matrix: run scenarios across Python/TS/Go where producer and consumer are mismatched versions.
Chaos tests: simulate network partitions and verify streaming reconnection and idempotent retry semantics.
Performance: measure 95th percentile added latency for shim path; target < 5ms overhead at median request size.
rollback_plan: Server: revert routing rules to previous behavior and unmap shim endpoints; monitor for immediate decrease in errors.
Clients: publish patch releases that re-enable legacy direct calls where shims introduced regressions.
Communication: notify customers via Console banner and status page; provide a support-runbook to assist customers who saw failures.
